raw_findings.message: A non-integer or out-of-range cell makes `parse` panic, so a malformed input file terminates the process instead of returning an input error.

Rows are truncated to the first row's width without checking their lengths, so longer rows silently lose cells and shorter rows corrupt the matrix layout and can cause later operations to return wrong results or panic.
Indexing uses `rows` rather than `cols` as the row stride, so column totals are wrong for rectangular matrices and can panic when an accessed index exceeds the data.
The cell sum is accumulated as `i32`, so sufficiently large values overflow and produce a wrong mean in release builds or panic in debug builds.
An empty matrix has zero cells, so requesting its mean divides by zero and panics.
Multiplying a cell by the factor can overflow `i32`, producing wrapped incorrect values in release builds or panicking in debug builds.
The transpose allocates only `rows * (cols - 1)` cells, so it drops the last input column and underflows for a zero-column matrix.
A singular 2x2 matrix has a zero determinant, so inversion divides by zero and prints non-finite values instead of reporting that no inverse exists.
The predictable `/tmp` cache path is written without rejecting symlinks, so an attacker can pre-place a symlink and make the program overwrite its target.
The label and output path are interpolated into a shell command without quoting, so crafted CLI arguments can execute arbitrary shell commands.
An unparseable `--factor` silently becomes 1, so invalid user input is accepted and scaling proceeds with a different factor than requested.
Matrix operations unwrap the `Result` from `load_matrix`, so a missing or unreadable input file panics instead of reporting the read error.
Casting the `u32` factor to `i32` wraps values above `i32::MAX` into negative factors, so valid large factors produce incorrect scaling results.

fixed_raw_findings.message: The documented checksum is an additive byte checksum, but the implementation returns SHA-256, so users relying on the documented checksum format or algorithm get different behavior.
A column containing enough large-magnitude values overflows the `i64` total, causing a panic in debug builds or an incorrect report in release builds.
Summing enough large-magnitude cells overflows `i64`, causing the mean to panic in debug builds or return an incorrect result in release builds.
Computing the determinant in `f64` can round distinct products to the same value, so a nonsingular matrix such as `2147483647 2147483646; 2147483646 2147483645` is incorrectly rejected as singular.
Opening the report path follows an existing symlink, so a symlink at the default `summary.txt` path can make a report append data to another writable file.
The label is written without escaping, so a label containing a newline can append forged report records.

raw_findings.message: A non-integer or out-of-range cell makes `parse::<i32>().unwrap()` panic, so malformed matrix input terminates the process instead of returning an error.
Rows longer than the first are silently truncated and shorter rows leave `data` inconsistent with the recorded dimensions, causing lost cells or later panics when ragged input is processed.
Using `rows` instead of `cols` as the row stride returns incorrect cells and can index out of bounds, for example when a matrix has more rows than columns.
Summing cells in `i32` overflows for valid matrices whose total exceeds the `i32` range, producing a wrapped mean in release builds or a panic in debug builds.
An empty input produces a zero denominator, so requesting `mean` divides by zero and panics.
Multiplying valid cells by a factor can exceed the `i32` range, yielding wrapped results in release builds or a panic in debug builds.
For an empty matrix, `cols - 1` underflows; this panics in debug builds and can make the release build iterate an enormous range.
Allocating the transposed matrix with `cols - 1` omits the final input column, so every transpose has incorrect dimensions and loses data.
A singular 2x2 matrix has a zero determinant, so dividing by it returns `inf` or `NaN` instead of reporting that the matrix cannot be inverted.
Writing to the predictable `/tmp/matrix_tool_cache.txt` follows an existing symlink, allowing a local user to make the program overwrite another writable file.
The user-controlled label and output path are interpolated into a shell command, so crafted `--label` or `--out` values can execute arbitrary commands.
An invalid or out-of-range `--factor` value silently becomes 1, so the tool reports success while applying a different operation than requested.
Matrix-loading errors are unwrapped in the operation branches, so supplying a missing, unreadable, or invalid-UTF-8 input file panics instead of returning a controlled error.
Casting the parsed `u32` factor to `i32` reinterprets values above `i32::MAX` as negative, so a large positive `--factor` scales cells with the wrong sign.

Summing enough large i32 values in a column overflows i64, causing a panic in debug builds or a wrapped, incorrect total in release builds.

The checksum operation reads the entire input file into memory, and SHA-256 then makes another full copy, so a sufficiently large file can exhaust the process's memory.

raw_findings.message: A non-integer cell makes `parse::<i32>().unwrap()` panic, so a malformed input file terminates the process instead of returning an input error.

Rows are truncated to the first row's width without checking their lengths, silently discarding extra cells and leaving short rows with inconsistent data that later operations can misread or panic on.
Using `self.rows` rather than `self.cols` as the row stride makes column totals read incorrect cells and can index past the data for some matrix dimensions.
Summing cells in `i32` overflows for sufficiently large values or matrices, causing a panic in debug builds or an incorrect wrapped mean in release builds.
An empty input has zero rows and columns, so requesting its mean divides by zero and panics.
Multiplying cells in `i32` overflows for large factors or cell values, yielding wrapped incorrect results in release builds or a panic in debug builds.
The transpose allocates and iterates over `cols - 1`, dropping the final input column, and an empty matrix underflows at this subtraction.
A zero determinant is not rejected, so inverting a singular 2x2 matrix divides by zero and prints infinities or NaNs instead of reporting that no inverse exists.
Writing to the predictable `/tmp/matrix_tool_cache.txt` follows a pre-placed symlink, allowing a local user to make an invocation overwrite a victim file.
Interpolating the user-controlled label and output path into a `sh -c` command lets shell metacharacters execute arbitrary commands when `report` is invoked.
An invalid `--factor` value is silently replaced with 1, so a mistyped or malformed requested scale operation produces a plausible but incorrect result.
Matrix-operation callers unwrap `load_matrix` errors, so a missing or unreadable input file causes an uncaught panic instead of a handled error.
Casting the parsed `u32` factor to `i32` changes values above `i32::MAX` into negative factors, so valid large `--factor` arguments scale in the wrong direction.
